overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the recess video shut-off did not show improper deliberation, and the executive session notice and chair's statement were sufficiently specific despite miscited statutory references.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged improper deliberations could have occurred off camera during a recess after the camera operator turned off the video broadcast.
allegations.key_passage: Absent evidence to the contrary, we credit the public body's version of events

allegations.summary: The video broadcast was shut off during the recess; the complaint argued this allowed off-camera discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Because a public body is not required to broadcast or record its meetings, then the camera operator's decision to turn off the video broadcast during a recess did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice gave insufficient detail for the May 10 executive session topics (real property and union contract negotiations).
allegations.key_passage: As long as a public body provides a sufficient description of the executive session

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair and notice misstated statutory citations, so the Board failed to follow proper procedure before convening in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: This level of detail regarding the topics to be discussed in executive session satisfied the Board's obligations under the Open Meeting Law.
